quotes.text: AI doesn't leak data accidentally. It leaks it correctly under bad identity design. AI doesn't create wrong answers randomly. It produces wrong answers deterministically when your enterprise cannot agree on truth.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shifts the blame for AI failures from the model to identity design and unresolved definitions.

quotes.text: Architecturally, AI is an accelerator. It does not create structure. It magnifies whatever structure already exists, your data quality, your identity boundaries, your decision rights, your exception culture, your cost discipline.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concisely frames AI as an amplifier of the existing operating model.

quotes.text: Cost surprises are architecture signals. They tell you where the operating model is missing boundaries where usage is unconstrained, where ownership is undefined and where self-service became unpriced consumption.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes AI cost spikes as design omissions rather than finance problems.

quotes.text: Data mesh without semantic contracts doesn't create agility. It creates scalable confusion and AI turns scalable confusion into automated decision damage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sharp warning about decentralizing data without shared definitions.

quotes.text: If you remember nothing else, don't govern AI by platform spend. Govern AI by unit economics, because platforms change. Operating models must survive.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives executives a vendor-independent way to steer AI investment.

chapters.title: The data platform as a product
Guardrails: identity, trust and semantic contracts
AI economics and cost per decision

takeaways: AI amplifies the existing operating model, so ownership of truth, access approvals and cost must be decided before a pilot scales.
Identity, classification and lineage, and semantic contracts must be deterministic layers so probabilistic AI components stay within a bounded blast radius.
Steer AI with unit economics such as cost per decision, each with a named business owner, plus time-bound, recorded exception pathways.
hook: Most AI pilots impress in the demo and then stall on untrusted answers, cost spikes and compliance panic. This episode is for CIOs, CDOs and platform leaders who need AI to survive production in the Microsoft ecosystem. You get a three-to-five-year operating model built on decision rights, guardrails, semantic contracts and unit economics.
